gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Lenovo Idea Tab Pro's USB-C port carries DisplayPort video to an external monitor and that its keyboard dock attaches by pogo pins. That makes it the only one of ChatGPT's sub-$1,000 picks that can drive a monitor, because the Galaxy Tab S10 FE's USB-C 2.0 port cannot.
standout_why: I read the one cited rival page, mynexttablet.com/best-tablets-keyboards. It already says the Tab S10 FE and S10 Lite have 'USB-C 2.0, no monitor output', that the Ultra has 'USB-C 3.2 with monitor output', and that the Tab S11 has 'No touchpad option'. It covers only Samsung models, so it says nothing about the Lenovo Idea Tab Pro's DisplayPort output or how its keyboard connects. It also never says how any keyboard attaches. The other cited rival is WIRED (three URLs), and the top result is Android Authority. I could not open either: WebFetch can't reach wired.com, and Android Authority returned HTTP 403. So I can't rule out that they mention Lenovo's DisplayPort output. This is new against the one cited page I could read, but it doesn't settle the pick by itself.
decides: If the shopper wants a keyboard tablet that also works at a desk with a monitor, the 'Best overall value' pick is wrong. Mynexttablet says the Tab S10 FE cannot output video at all. That means the cheapest pick in ChatGPT's lineup that can drive a monitor is the Lenovo Idea Tab Pro, at $449.99 per ChatGPT's card (I did not open a store page to confirm this). Notebookcheck documents DisplayPort output and a pogo-pin keyboard dock for it. Above that price, the only Samsung that Samsung itself says pairs with an external monitor (DeX Extended Mode) is the Tab S11 Ultra. Samsung's UK support page names only the Ultra for this, not the base Tab S11. For a shopper who just types on the tablet screen, this doesn't change the pick. Every keyboard here attaches by pogo pins, so none needs Bluetooth pairing.

It also says the software 'automatically switches to a mode optimized for this control when a mouse and keyboard are connected.' The review's keyboard price (about $80 at online retailers) dates from early 2025, so I left it out as a current price.
